That builds the sample house and saves the project, an IFC4 file and the Level 1 plan:

`--cmd 'render {"view": "{3D}", "path": "house-3d.png"}'` adds the 3D view (`azimuth` and `elevation` turn it); `render {"view": "Section 1"}` draws the sample's section, `South` (or `North`, `East`, `West`) one of its elevations, and `render {"view": "A102"}` one of its sheets. `--save sheets.pdf` prints every sheet, a page each. A script is one command per line, `id {json params}`, with lengths in millimetres: ```text wall {"points": [[0,0],[8000,0],[8000,6000],[0,6000]], "closed": true, "type": "Exterior - 300mm"} door {"at": [2000, 0]} window {"at": [8000, 3000]} room {"point": [4000, 3000], "name": "Living"} floor {} roof {} ``` A script stops at its first failing line and names it. Through MCP, `script {"text": …, "atomic": true}` runs it all or nothing: a line that fails takes back the lines before it, and one that goes through is a single undo step. ```sh bimcraft-cli run --script house.txt --save house.ifc bimcraft-cli convert building.ifc building.bimcraft # an IFC file from Revit or any BIM tool, as a project bimcraft-cli info house.bimcraft # levels, counts, types and warnings bimcraft-cli info building.rvt # a Revit file: release, last save, levels, elements by category bimcraft-cli convert building.rvt building.ifc # a Revit project, imported, then written as IFC4 bimcraft-cli convert house.bimcraft plan.svg bimcraft-cli commands # every command and its parameters ``` ## The desktop app `bimcraft [FILE] [--sample]` opens a `.bimcraft` project, imports an `.ifc` file, or starts on the sample house. The layout is Revit's, so it should feel familiar: the Quick Access Toolbar; the ribbon's File, Architecture, Annotate, View and Modify tabs, with a green contextual tab (Modify | Place Wall, Modify | Walls) for the tool or the selection; the Options Bar; Properties over the Project Browser; views in tabs with a navigation bar; and the tool's prompt in the status bar. The icons and colours are BIMCraft's own: BIMCraft starts in your system's theme. View > Dark Mode opens a menu for Light, Dark, Dark UI, Light Canvas, or As the System; File > Settings offers the same choices. The choice is saved between sessions. Autosave runs in the background every two minutes while the model has unsaved changes (File > Settings > Files changes the interval or disables it). A saved project's recovery copy is `.autosave.bimcraft` beside the project; an untitled project's copy is under the system temporary folder's `bimcraft-autosave` directory. Opening a project with a copy offers **Recover**, **Discard**, or **Postpone**. Recover opens unsaved work, Discard removes the copy, and Postpone protects it for later through File > Recover Autosave. Orphaned untitled copies are offered at startup. Successful Save or an explicit Don't Save removes the current recovery copy, except a postponed copy. See [autosave design](docs/autosave.md). | To | Do | |---|---| | Draw walls | Wall (WA), click points: each click builds a wall from the point before, one undo step each; Enter or Esc ends the chain, and a click back on its start closes it. Ends snap to wall ends and location lines; Shift keeps a segment square. The Draw panel draws a Line, or a Start-End-Radius Arc: its start, its end, then a point it passes through. The Options Bar sets the height (up to a level, or unconnected), the Location Line (the line of the wall you click along) and Chain. A wall's exterior is to your left as you go, so draw clockwise for walls that face out | | Flip, attach walls | Select walls, and Modify \| Walls has Flip (or Space) to turn their exterior side round about their location line, Attach Top/Base to pick a roof or a floor for their tops (or, as the Options Bar says, their bases) to follow, and Detach Top/Base. Properties shows their Location Line (pick another and the wall stays where it is) and whether they're attached | | Place doors, windows | Door (DR) or Window (WN), click a wall; the Type Selector at the top of Properties picks the type. Before the click the door or window is sketched in the wall under the cursor, with how far it stands from each end of the wall | | Place rooms | Room (RM), click inside walls; the outline and area show before you click, and the tag's area follows the walls | | Place columns | Column (CL), click where it stands; it snaps to wall ends and centre lines. The Options Bar sets how high it goes (up to a level, or unconnected), the Type Selector rectangular or round | | Plumbing tab | Plumbing > Pipe (PI), Plumbing Fixture (PX), Pipe Fitting (PF), Pipe Accessory (PA). A pipe takes two clicks or a chain of them, as a beam does; the Options Bar sets its justification (the middle by default) and its height over the level, and Properties its two heights, so a drain falls and a riser rises. A fixture, a fitting or a valve is a family's type where you click, the Type Selector listing only the families of its kind, Space turning it. Edit Type of a pipe sets its diameter, whether it is round and its material | | Electrical tab | Electrical > Electrical Equipment (EE), Device (DV), Lighting Fixture (LF), and Conduit & Wire > Conduit (CN), Cable Tray (CT), Wire (EW). A run takes two clicks or a chain, as a pipe does, its Options Bar the justification (the middle) and the height; a board, a device or a luminaire is a family's type where you click, the Type Selector listing only the families of its kind (an outlet and a switch under Device), Space turning it. Edit Type of a tray sets its width and depth, of a conduit or a wire its diameter | | Lightning Protection tab | Lightning Protection > Air Terminal (AT), Down Conductor (DC), Earthing Electrode (EG), Inspection Box (IB), Earthing Conductor (GC): free letters, since Revit has none. Runs and fixtures as the other tabs'; the vocabulary is the standard's (captor, condutor de descida, haste de aterramento, caixa de inspeção, condutor de aterramento) | | Data tab | Data > Data Outlet (DT), Voice Outlet (VO), Rack (RK), Patch Panel (PN), and Cabling > Cable Tray (CT, the Electrical tab's), Cabling (CB). Free letters where Revit has none; the Type Selector lists only the families of the tool's kind | | Structure tab | Structure > Column (CL on this tab; Revit's own), Beam (BM), Floor: Structural (SB), and Foundation > Isolated Footing (FI), Wall Footing (FW; Revit's FT is Filters here), and Reinforcement > Reinforce (RF, ours: it arms the element selected; RB is the Massing tab's Roof by Face). A beam or a wall footing takes two clicks, or a chain of them (Options Bar > Chain), each step a beam; the Options Bar sets a beam's justification (top, centre or bottom) and its height over the level, a footing's thickness and where its top is, a structural column's height. The tool sketches what the click would make and the beam's length; a beam seen under, over or through the plan is picked by its centre line; Properties shows its Start and End Level Offset, Z Justification and System, and Edit Type its section. A structural floor is the Floor tool with its `structural` flag | | Add stairs, ramps | Stair: click where it starts (the middle of its first riser), then where its run ends. Past the end of a run of all its risers, it climbs to the level above in one run; short of it, a landing follows, and the next click says which way the next run goes from it: on, left, right, or back beside the last. Risers are at most 180 mm; the Options Bar sets its width and Railings, Properties its riser, tread and top. Ramp: the same clicks, its runs as long as the Options Bar's slope makes them, as high as its Height says | | Add railings | Railing: click a stair or a ramp for a railing down each side, or click a path's points and press Enter for one along it on the plan's level; the Type Selector picks its type, Type Properties its height and baluster spacing | | Roof the building | Roof, in a plan: click inside the walls, and a roof goes on the level above, over their outline and past their faces, whatever its shape, and open over a courtyard: a loop of walls standing free inside the others, with no room in it; its hips and valleys show before you click. The Options Bar sets the slope (0° for a flat roof), the overhang, and gable ends for a rectangle. Select a roof, and Modify \| Roofs has Gable Edge: click an edge of its footprint (a courtyard's too) to stand it upright, a gable end, and again to slope it. Roof by Extrusion: click a line's start and end, then how far across the roof is swept; its profile rises from the line at the Options Bar's slope to a ridge over its middle, or with Shed along its whole length | | Dormers | Architecture > Opening > Dormer: click a roof's slope where the dormer's front wall goes; the Options Bar sets its width, its height over the roof at the front, its roof's slope and whether its front has a window. Its walls stand on the roof, its own gable roof runs back into the host, and the host opens under it | | Floors, slopes | Floor: click inside the walls, and a slab goes under their outline, open over a courtyard (a loop of walls standing free inside the others, with no room in it), its top at the level; Properties sets its Height Offset From Level. Selected, Shape Editing > Slope Arrow: click its tail, then its head, and the floor rises toward the head at the Options Bar's slope; Properties changes the slope | | Ceilings | Ceiling: click inside a room, and a ceiling fills it out to its walls' faces, open round any walls standing free inside it, at the Options Bar's height (2600 mm); the outline shows before you click, and the Type Selector picks a plain one or tiles. The Project Browser's Ceiling Plans open each level's reflected ceiling plan | | Shafts | Architecture > Opening > Shaft: click two opposite corners; the Options Bar sets how high it goes (up to a level, or unconnected). It cuts the floors, ceilings and roofs on its way | | Masses | Massing > Conceptual Mass > Mass (MS): click the footprint's corners; the Options Bar sets how high it goes (up to a level, or unconnected); Enter, or the first corner again, finishes. Before you do, the outline it would make shows, with its area. With a mass selected, Model by Face makes Mass Floors (MF: a floor at each level it crosses), Wall by Face (WB: a wall on each edge), Floor by Face (FB) and Roof by Face (RB) on its top face, and Update to Face (UF) makes what they made follow the mass again; Show Mass (MH) hides and shows masses in the view on screen. Properties shows its constraints, its Top Outline (corners as `x, y; x, y`, blank for none: typed, the mass is lofted), area, volume and gross floor area. View > Schedules lists Mass and Mass Floor schedules | | Add levels, grids | Level (LL) takes an elevation in the Options Bar; Grid (GR) takes two clicks | | Select | Click; Ctrl adds, Shift takes away, Tab reaches what's underneath (the wall under a door). Drag across empty floor for a box: left to right takes what's wholly inside, right to left what it crosses too; in a section or an elevation, any drag draws one. The selection stays as you open other views, the 3D view and schedules among them | | Edit, delete | Properties edits the parameters of everything selected, in one step, grouped as Revit groups them; the Type Selector changes the type; Delete removes the selection | | Move, copy | Drag a selected element, or Move (MV) and Copy (CO): click a base point, then where it goes. Walls joined to a moved wall stretch to stay joined, so room areas follow; doors and windows slide along their walls. Constrain keeps the move square; Multiple goes on copying | | Rotate, mirror | Rotate (RO) turns the selection about its middle: click the angle's start, then its end, or type an angle in the Options Bar; Place Centre moves the centre. Mirror Pick Axis (MM) mirrors across a wall or grid you pick, Mirror Draw Axis (DM) across a line you click; Copy is on, as in Revit | | Align, trim, split, offset | Align (AL): hover to highlight an edge or centre line, pick the reference, then the target edge. It turns and moves walls, columns, components, slabs, roofs, structural/MEP runs and detail geometry onto the reference in one undo step; hosted doors and windows slide along their wall. While sketching, align sketch lines to model edges or other sketch lines; joined endpoints follow, with sketch undo until Finish. Trim/Extend to Corner (TR): pick two walls on the parts to keep. Split Element (SL): click a wall where to cut it. Offset (OF): point to a wall, and a copy goes to the cursor's side at the Options Bar's distance | | Dimension, tag | Annotate > Aligned (DI): pick parallel references, each the line nearest the cursor (a wall's face, centre line or end, a door's or window's centre or jamb, a grid), or endpoints (a wall's end or corner, a line's or a grid's end), which a square marks, then click away from them where the dimension line goes; more picks make a chain. Linear: pick endpoints, then click where it goes, horizontal or vertical as the cursor lies; the Options Bar's Place (Auto, Aligned, Horizontal, Vertical; Space steps them) lays either tool's dimension. Angular: pick two lines that meet, then click where the arc goes; the angle on that side. Radial and Diameter: pick a round column, a curved wall, a circle or an arc, then click where it goes. Arc Length: pick a curved wall or an arc, then, to measure part of it, two ends on it, then click where the dimension's arc goes. Edit Type on a dimension opens Dimension Type Properties; a double click on one of its numbers opens Dimension Text, that segment's own prefix, suffix, text above and below, or text in its place. Selected, a dimension shows a padlock under each segment and EQ past its end: a click locks a segment at its length, or keeps the segments equal, and what it measures to then moves with what moves, as in Revit. Annotate > Tag by Category (TG): click any element with a place in a plan (a door or window, a wall, a column, a component, a floor, ceiling or roof, a room, a beam or pipe, a stair) to tag it with its type, a door's or window's with its mark, a room's with its name, or with any other field its schedule has (Height, Area, a project parameter) typed in Label in the Options Bar, with a leader when it says so; Tag All tags the doors and windows of the view not tagged yet. Drag a dimension or a tag to move it | | Spot elevations, text | Annotate > Spot Elevation (EL): click a floor, a roof, a stair or a wall in plan, and it reads the height of its top there, following it; in a section, click a point to mark its height. Annotate > Text (TX): type the note in the Options Bar (`\n` breaks a line), then click its top left corner, in a plan, a section or on a sheet; Properties sets its size and angle | | Crop, view range | View > Crop View crops a plan or a section to what it shows; drag the grips at its edges' middles to move them (a section's sides move its line). Off shows it all again: a section or an elevation, all there is along its line, past its ends. Properties of a plan holds its View Range: Top (clear it for the level above), Cut Plane, Bottom and View Depth, in mm above the level | | Filled regions | Annotate > Filled Region (FR) and Masking Region start a boundary sketch. Edit Type opens Type Properties for a selected region or the current sketch: duplicate and rename types; choose foreground and background patterns and colors separately; set masking; check the combined preview. A pattern's … button opens the patterns, to create and edit them. Apply/OK save the draft as one undo step; Cancel drops unapplied work. A type change updates every region using it; the palette's Type Selector controls the instance's type. Non-masking fills keep cut foreground patterns and projected model lines visible; masking fills cover the model. Sketches snap to visible model edges, detail lines, existing region boundaries and their own geometry, with the configured snaps and angle guides. | | Visibility/Graphics | View > Visibility/Graphics (VV, VG) opens the active view's dialog, a table as Revit's: a row for each model category (searched by name, with All, None and Invert, and Object Styles… for what isn't overridden), its visibility, then Projection/Surface Lines, Patterns and Transparency, Cut Lines and Patterns, each cell showing what it overrides (the line as it draws, the fill's colour, the percent) and opening its own small dialog (lines: a colour, weight and dash, each with a box that turns it on; patterns: a fill colour; transparency, seen in 3D; Clear Overrides), Halftone a box in the row, and Detail Level, By View until a category can have its own; the Annotation Categories have their lines and halftone; Filters applies the project's filters in order, each a row alike, with Add, Remove, Up and Down; Elements lists what's hidden or overridden one by one. Design Options picks which option of each set the view shows (the primary unless it chooses). OK and Apply send what changed as one `graphics` command, one undo step; Cancel drops it. A view that follows a view template shows what the template controls, and leaves it be | | Hide in View | Select, then Modify > View: Hide Element (EH) leaves the elements out of the view, Hide Category (VH) every category the selection is of, Override Graphics (EO) opens Visibility/Graphics on its Elements tab with the selection added. Unhide Elements (EU) opens that tab, with what's hidden; tick a box to bring it back | | Temporary hide and isolate | The view control bar under a plan, a section or the 3D view: Temporary Hide/Isolate hides the selected elements (HH) or their categories (HC), or isolates them (HI) or their categories (IC), in that view only, and Reset (HR) brings it all back; the view wears a cyan frame meanwhile. The four hide and isolate items are greyed out until something is selected, as in Revit. Apply Hide/Isolate to View makes it the view's own, as one undo step. Reveal Hidden Elements (RH) draws what the view hides for good in magenta, and again hides it. None of this is saved or undone: it is the window's | | Scale, detail level, visual style | The view control bar's first buttons. In a plan, a section or an elevation, Scale lists 1 : 1 to 1 : 1000, or in a project in feet and inches the architect's scales (12" = 1'-0" to 1/32" = 1'-0") and the engineer's (1" = 10'-0" to 1" = 200'-0"), and takes any other typed in Custom, as n, 1 : n or `1/4" = 1'-0"` (every view has one: 1 : 100, or 1/8" = 1'-0" in feet and inches, until it is given another, and its annotation and line weights are the paper's at that scale); Detail Level picks Coarse, Medium or Fine. 419	
420	Each of these runs a command, so what you do in the window is checked, undone and saved exactly as from the CLI or an agent.
421	
422	## Drive it from agents, MCP and the CLI
423	
424	`bimcraft-cli mcp` serves the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) over stdio, on a model of its own.
425	Add it to Claude Code:
426	
427	```sh
428	claude mcp add bimcraft -- /path/to/bimcraft-cli mcp
429	```
430	
431	or to any MCP client's configuration:
432	
433	```json
434	{ "mcpServers": { "bimcraft": { "command": "/path/to/bimcraft-cli", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
435	```
436	
437	| Tool | What it does |
438	|---|---|
439	| `execute {command, params}` | Any command with JSON parameters |
440	| `script {text, atomic?}` | Several commands, one per line; `atomic`: all or nothing, one undo step |
441	| `list_commands {filter?}` | The catalog, with parameters and shortcuts |
442	| `inspect_model` | Levels, counts, types, warnings and undo history |
443	| `query_elements {category?, level?}` | Elements with derived values: wall length and height, room area, door position |
444	| `schedule {name?, category?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?}` | A schedule's columns, rows and totals; a new one, or one changed, as the command makes it |
445	| `render {view?, ceiling?, width?, height?, azimuth?, elevation?}` | A level's floor plan (or reflected ceiling plan), a section or elevation by name, a sheet by number, or with `view: "{3D}"` the 3D view, as a PNG the agent can look at |
446	| `new_model`, `open`, `save` | Projects; `open` imports `.ifc` files, `save` to `.ifc`, `.svg` or `.png` exports |
447	
448	A command that fails comes back as a tool error saying what to fix (`door: no wall at [4000, 3000] on Level 1`), and it
449	changes nothing.
450	
451	### On the project you have open
452	
453	Start the window with `--control PORT` (`0` for any free port) and an agent can work on the project in front of you instead of
454	a copy of its own: what it makes appears in the window, as an undo step you can take back, and is saved with Ctrl+S.
455	
456	```sh
457	bimcraft --control 0                       # the window says the port; bridge.json beside the favorites holds it and a token
458	claude mcp add bimcraft -- /path/to/bimcraft-cli mcp --connect
459	```
460	
461	`mcp --connect` takes the port from that file (or `--connect PORT` names it, which must be the window's). The port is on this
462	machine's own address only, a connection that does not say the token in its first line is dropped, and only the user can read
463	the file. The tools are the same, except `new_model` and `open`, which would replace your project: start or open another in
464	the window. The window answers between its frames, so a long command holds the window as it would from a button.
465	
466	File > Settings > Agents opens the same port without `--control` (and again at each start), on a port you choose or any free one,
467	and closes it. With **Allow agents to edit this project** off, an agent only reads your project: it inspects it, reads its schedules,
468	renders its views and exports it to new files (the sheets to PDF among them), and every change it asks for comes back as an error
469	that says so. The view control bar shows the port: off, listening on its number, or how many agents are connected, and read-only.
470	An agent's own side can ask the same: `bimcraft-cli mcp --connect --read-only`, or `bimcraft-cli mcp --read-only house.bimcraft`
471	for a headless server that opens the file and then only reads it.
472	
473	## Commands
474	
475	| Command | Shortcut | Parameters |
476	|---|---|---|
477	| `autosave` | | `path`: atomically write a native recovery snapshot without changing the project path or undo history |
478	| `recover` | | `path`, `project?`: validate and open a recovery snapshot; later Save targets `project`, or asks for Save As without it |
479	| `wall` | WA | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `top_offset?` (mm above `top_level`, negative below it), `height?`, `base_offset?`, `arc?` (degrees each turns, counter-clockwise), `location?` (`centre`, `core-centre`, `exterior-finish`, `interior-finish`, `exterior-core`, `interior-core`), `attach_top?`, `attach_base?` (a roof or a floor), `room_bounding?` (false: rooms run past it, as Revit's Room Bounding off; `modify` turns it on and off) |
480	| `door` | DR | `at`, or `wall` and `offset?`; `type?`, `family?` (a door family's `type`, its first by default), `mark?`, `flip_facing?`, `flip_hand?` |
481	| `window` | WN | as `door`, plus `sill?` (a family's `Sill Height` by default) |
482	| `sketch` | | `lines` ([[[x, y], [x, y]], …]; an arc [[x, y], [x, y], [x, y]], its ends then a point it passes through): solves a sketch without making anything, the loops it closes into (outlines and their holes) and their area, or every problem with the lines it's about: ends no other line meets, lines that intersect or overlap (a line that crosses itself too), three or more lines at a point. A sketch is solved as the straight pieces its lines are drawn with (an arc or a circle is cut into chords): past 200,000 of them it is refused at once |
483	| `edit_boundary` | | `id` (a floor, a ceiling, a roof by footprint or a shaft), `sketch?`: its outline and holes redrawn as one sketch, a line sent back with its `id` keeping it; without `sketch`, the lines it has now, each with its id once it has one |
484	| `floor` | | `boundary?` (else the walls of the level) or `sketch?` (lines, in any order, solved into its outline and openings), `openings?` (holes in it, inside it and apart; over the walls, by default each loop of them standing free inside, joined to none of the outer ones and with no room in it), `level?`, `type?`, `offset?` (its top above the level), `slope?` (degrees) and `arrow?` (its tail and head: it rises from the tail toward the head), `structural?` (a floor that carries load, as Revit's Floor: Structural). Its model pattern starts at `pattern_origin` and turns by `pattern_angle` (set with `modify`) |
485	| `ceiling` | | `point` (in a room: out to its walls' faces, open round the walls standing free inside it), `boundary` or `sketch`, `openings?` (holes in it, inside it and apart), `level?`, `type?`, `offset?` (its underside above the level, 2600) |
486	| `shaft` | | `boundary` or `sketch`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `height?`, `base_offset?`: a hole through the floors, ceilings and roofs on its way |
487	| `room` | RM | `point`, `name?`, `number?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `limit_offset?`, `base_offset?`, `frozen?` (keeps its boundary: it isn't found from the walls again) |
488	| `room_separator` | | `points` [[x, y], …], `level?`, `closed?`: room separation lines, one per segment, that bound rooms where there is no wall (an open plan) and nothing else |
489	| `column` | CL | `at`, `type?`, `angle?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `height?`, `base_offset?` |
490	| `structural_column` | CL | as `column`, in its own category and types |
491	| `reinforcement_preset` | | `name?`, `kind?` (beam, column, footing, floor), `params?` (what `reinforce` takes, but the host), `rename?`, `delete?`: a named set of parameters, kept in the project; no `name` lists them |
492	| `voltage` | | `name?`, `nominal?` (volts), `min?`, `max?` (the band a device may read within; 10 per cent either way unless given), `rename?`, `delete?`: a voltage of the electrical settings; one a distribution system supplies cannot be deleted; no `name` lists them |
493	| `distribution_system` | | `name?`, `phases?` (1, 2, 3), `wires?` (the line conductors and the neutral), `l_l?`, `l_n?`, `l_g?` (names of voltages; "" takes one away), `ground?` (TN-S, TN-C, TN-C-S, TT, IT), `rename?`, `delete?`: a distribution system of the electrical settings; a voltage the project lacks is refused; no `name` lists them |
494	| `wire_type` | | `name?`, `material?` (copper, aluminium), `temperature?` (°C), `insulation?`, `note?`, `sizes?` (`[{section, ampacity, label?}]`, mm² and amperes, which replaces the table), `rename?`, `delete?`: a wire type of the electrical settings; no `name` lists them |
495	| `reinforce` | | `host` (a beam, a column, a footing or a floor) or `hosts` (a list), `preset?`, `cover?`, `grade?`, `grade_stirrup?`, `clearance?`, and by host: `bottom`, `top`, `stirrup`, `skin`, `anchor` (beam), `bars`, `stirrup`, `ties`, `anchor` (column), `mesh` (footing), `bottom`, `top` (floor), `check?`, `aggressiveness?`, `fck?`: bars by rules, as `rebar` elements on layers, and notes from the check |
496	| `footing` | FI | `at`, `type?`, `thickness?` (400), `offset?` (its top over the level, 0), `angle?`, `level?`: an isolated footing |
497	| `beam` | BM | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `offset?` (the height of its `justify` line over the level at its start, 0), `end_offset?` (at its end, for one segment: it slopes), `justify?` (`top`, `centre`, `bottom`), `system?`: a beam for each segment |
498	| `pipe` | PI | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `offset?` (the height of its `justify` line over the level at its start, 0), `end_offset?` (at its end, for one segment: it falls or rises, or stands if the two points are one), `justify?` (`centre` by default), `system?`: a pipe for each segment |
499	| `conduit` | CN | as `pipe`: a conduit (eletroduto) for each segment, round |
500	| `cable_tray` | CT | as `pipe`, its type a `width` across by a `depth` deep: a cable tray (eletrocalha) for each segment |
501	| `wire` | EW | as `pipe`: a wire (condutor) for each segment, round; its `system` the circuit |
502	| `down_conductor` | DC | as `pipe`: a down conductor (condutor de descida) for each segment; the same point twice and two heights stand it upright |

Each of these runs a command, so what you do in the window is checked, undone and saved exactly as from the CLI or an agent.

## Drive it from agents, MCP and the CLI

`bimcraft-cli mcp` serves the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) over stdio, on a model of its own.
Add it to Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add bimcraft -- /path/to/bimcraft-cli mcp
```

or to any MCP client's configuration:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "bimcraft": { "command": "/path/to/bimcraft-cli", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `execute {command, params}` | Any command with JSON parameters |
| `script {text, atomic?}` | Several commands, one per line; `atomic`: all or nothing, one undo step |
| `list_commands {filter?}` | The catalog, with parameters and shortcuts |
| `inspect_model` | Levels, counts, types, warnings and undo history |
| `query_elements {category?, level?}` | Elements with derived values: wall length and height, room area, door position |
| `schedule {name?, category?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?}` | A schedule's columns, rows and totals; a new one, or one changed, as the command makes it |
| `render {view?, ceiling?, width?, height?, azimuth?, elevation?}` | A level's floor plan (or reflected ceiling plan), a section or elevation by name, a sheet by number, or with `view: "{3D}"` the 3D view, as a PNG the agent can look at |
| `new_model`, `open`, `save` | Projects; `open` imports `.ifc` files, `save` to `.ifc`, `.svg` or `.png` exports |

A command that fails comes back as a tool error saying what to fix (`door: no wall at [4000, 3000] on Level 1`), and it
changes nothing.

### On the project you have open

Start the window with `--control PORT` (`0` for any free port) and an agent can work on the project in front of you instead of
a copy of its own: what it makes appears in the window, as an undo step you can take back, and is saved with Ctrl+S.

```sh
bimcraft --control 0                       # the window says the port; bridge.json beside the favorites holds it and a token
claude mcp add bimcraft -- /path/to/bimcraft-cli mcp --connect
```

`mcp --connect` takes the port from that file (or `--connect PORT` names it, which must be the window's). The port is on this
machine's own address only, a connection that does not say the token in its first line is dropped, and only the user can read
the file. The tools are the same, except `new_model` and `open`, which would replace your project: start or open another in
the window. The window answers between its frames, so a long command holds the window as it would from a button.

File > Settings > Agents opens the same port without `--control` (and again at each start), on a port you choose or any free one,
and closes it. With **Allow agents to edit this project** off, an agent only reads your project: it inspects it, reads its schedules,
renders its views and exports it to new files (the sheets to PDF among them), and every change it asks for comes back as an error
that says so. The view control bar shows the port: off, listening on its number, or how many agents are connected, and read-only.
An agent's own side can ask the same: `bimcraft-cli mcp --connect --read-only`, or `bimcraft-cli mcp --read-only house.bimcraft`
for a headless server that opens the file and then only reads it.

|---|---|---|
| `autosave` | | `path`: atomically write a native recovery snapshot without changing the project path or undo history |
| `recover` | | `path`, `project?`: validate and open a recovery snapshot; later Save targets `project`, or asks for Save As without it |
| `wall` | WA | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `top_offset?` (mm above `top_level`, negative below it), `height?`, `base_offset?`, `arc?` (degrees each turns, counter-clockwise), `location?` (`centre`, `core-centre`, `exterior-finish`, `interior-finish`, `exterior-core`, `interior-core`), `attach_top?`, `attach_base?` (a roof or a floor), `room_bounding?` (false: rooms run past it, as Revit's Room Bounding off; `modify` turns it on and off) |

602	## Roadmap
603	
604	Done: views and notes (view ranges, crop regions, text notes, spot elevations, angular and radial dimensions and dimensions to
605	wall ends and openings, schedules and the 3D view on sheets), project units (metric, or feet and inches), Portuguese and
606	Spanish, for the desktop and for projects, real walls (compound types with layers, joins at any angle, curved walls,
607	walls attached to roofs and floors, other location lines), sloped floors with openings, ceilings with openings and reflected ceiling plans, and shaft
608	openings, stairs of several runs with landings, ramps and railings, and roofs over any footprint (hips and valleys, gable
609	ends, courtyards), extrusion roofs and dormers, materials, with floors, roofs and ceilings built of layers as walls
610	are, families, BIMCraft's own parametric components (never Autodesk's `.rfa`), and project parameters and schedules with
611	chosen fields, filters, sorting and formulas, and visibility and graphics (overrides, view filters, view templates, phases and design options, which go out to IFC and come back), and families done: revolves and voids, doors and windows as families, the Family Editor, textures by material or from pictures you add, Paint, and favorites kept for every project, and updates (a check at startup, and the Windows installer's copy, an AppImage and the macOS app upgrading themselves).
612	Next, in order: locked and equal dimensions, arrays and groups; fill patterns of your own; DXF and DWG export, more of
613	IFC, and gbXML; the rest of structure (beams, columns, footings and structural floors are in), then MEP (its four tabs are designed in [docs/disciplines.md](docs/disciplines.md)); site and massing; several people editing one model; and signed installers (macOS
614	signing and notarization are wired up, waiting on a Developer ID). Revit's own `.rvt` format has no public specification, so BIMCraft reads it only through a reader of its own under the fence in
615	[docs/rvt-provenance.md](docs/rvt-provenance.md): it lists what a file holds (`bimcraft-cli info`) and imports its levels, walls, floors, doors
616	and windows, columns, rooms and roofs into a project, from the command line and from the desktop's File > Open, listing what was left out and why.

627	The installer is a short setup wizard. It puts BIMCraft and `bimcraft-cli` for every user in `Program Files\BIMCraft`, or in
628	the folder you pick on its folder page (Change, on any drive), adds BIMCraft to the Start menu, asks whether to put it on the
629	desktop too, opens `.bimcraft` projects in it, and offers it under Open with for `.ifc` files. It needs no Visual C++
630	runtime, and a newer version upgrades an older one, keeping the folder and the desktop shortcut as they were. For a silent
631	install with a desktop shortcut, in a folder of your own: `msiexec /i bimcraft-<ver>-windows-x64.msi /qn DESKTOPSHORTCUT=1
632	INSTALLFOLDER="D:\Apps\BIMCraft"`. It isn't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen asks before it runs: More info, then Run anyway.

634	The portable zip is for a PC where you can't install software: unzip it anywhere (a USB stick will do) and run `bimcraft.exe`.

637	either. BIMCraft only replaces the installer's copy in Program Files by itself, so a portable copy is told of a newer version

## Roadmap

Done: views and notes (view ranges, crop regions, text notes, spot elevations, angular and radial dimensions and dimensions to
wall ends and openings, schedules and the 3D view on sheets), project units (metric, or feet and inches), Portuguese and
Spanish, for the desktop and for projects, real walls (compound types with layers, joins at any angle, curved walls,
walls attached to roofs and floors, other location lines), sloped floors with openings, ceilings with openings and reflected ceiling plans, and shaft
openings, stairs of several runs with landings, ramps and railings, and roofs over any footprint (hips and valleys, gable
ends, courtyards), extrusion roofs and dormers, materials, with floors, roofs and ceilings built of layers as walls
are, families, BIMCraft's own parametric components (never Autodesk's `.rfa`), and project parameters and schedules with
chosen fields, filters, sorting and formulas, and visibility and graphics (overrides, view filters, view templates, phases and design options, which go out to IFC and come back), and families done: revolves and voids, doors and windows as families, the Family Editor, textures by material or from pictures you add, Paint, and favorites kept for every project, and updates (a check at startup, and the Windows installer's copy, an AppImage and the macOS app upgrading themselves).
Next, in order: locked and equal dimensions, arrays and groups; fill patterns of your own; DXF and DWG export, more of
IFC, and gbXML; the rest of structure (beams, columns, footings and structural floors are in), then MEP (its four tabs are designed in [docs/disciplines.md](docs/disciplines.md)); site and massing; several people editing one model; and signed installers (macOS
signing and notarization are wired up, waiting on a Developer ID). Revit's own `.rvt` format has no public specification, so BIMCraft reads it only through a reader of its own under the fence in
[docs/rvt-provenance.md](docs/rvt-provenance.md): it lists what a file holds (`bimcraft-cli info`) and imports its levels, walls, floors, doors
and windows, columns, rooms and roofs into a project, from the command line and from the desktop's File > Open, listing what was left out and why.

## The risk, stated plainly

The project owner chose this on 2026-10-21 and accepted the risk below. None of it is a legal conclusion.

- The agent that wrote this reader is not a lawyer. It did not verify rvt-rs's claim that its work is clean-room, and it makes
  no claim of its own about whether reading Revit's format is lawful in any country, or whether Autodesk's terms for Revit or
  for its sample files allow it. Those are the owner's to decide, with counsel if they want it.
- rvt-rs has one author. Its `CLEANROOM.md` describes a process (accepted and forbidden sources, a declaration on each pull
  request). Whether that process was followed was not audited here, and could not be from the outside.
- Some of rvt-rs's findings are second-hand: it credits Discussion #112 of its own repository (a user, STE1200), puzzbobb's
  measurements across 30 files, and `ahzs645/reviter`, whose "ODA loader analysis" is named as the independent source of the
  stored-page constants in `compression.rs`. What those people used to find them was not checked. Where this reader uses such a
  finding, the row says so and says how it was confirmed here (by the bytes of a sample file), which shows the finding is true
  and does not show where it came from. The stored-page constants are the exception: they were derived again from the bytes
  alone, by someone who had not seen them (see their section below).
- Autodesk's sample projects were downloaded from Autodesk's own public download host (see Sample files). Their terms of use
  were not checked.

## The fence

1. **A crate of its own.** `crates/rvt`, package `bimcraft-rvt`, `license = "Apache-2.0"` (not the repository's
   MIT OR Apache-2.0, because it holds Apache-2.0 code ported from rvt-rs). `bimcraft-core` never depends on it, and neither
   does `crates/update`, `crates/ui-egui` or the MCP server's core path. The command line (`apps/bimcraft-cli`) and the desktop
   (`apps/bimcraft`) take it through the Cargo feature `rvt`, which is on by default; a build without it is
   `--no-default-features`. A test reads the manifests (`crates/rvt/src/tests.rs`).
2. **Attribution, as Apache-2.0 asks.** `crates/rvt/LICENSE` is the licence text; `crates/rvt/NOTICE` carries rvt-rs's
   copyright line (Copyright 2026 Griffin Long) and says what was taken; every file with ported code opens with a header that
   names the rvt-rs source file and commit and says it was changed. A build that includes the crate is distributed under
   Apache-2.0: the README says so, every package (deb, rpm, Arch, AppImage, the AppStream metainfo, the Windows installer and the
   macOS bundle) names Apache-2.0, and each ships the root `NOTICE`, which starts with a copy of the crate's (a test keeps it
   so) and goes on to the interface fonts' notice.
3. **This document.** Every module and every format finding has a source from the accepted list below.
4. **Nothing inside an Autodesk file becomes BIMCraft content.** No family, template, icon or help text is bundled, extracted
   or shipped. The reader reads a file the user gives it. Test fixtures are synthetic files written by the tests; Autodesk's
   files are never committed.
5. **The policy documents say so.** CLAUDE.md's clean-room rule and principle 5 of the roadmap point here.

### Accepted sources

1. Public specifications: MS-CFB (the Compound File Binary format, which Revit files are), RFC 1951 and RFC 1952 (deflate and
   gzip), the PNG specification, and for the schema of the model, IFC4 (ISO 16739).
2. Byte observations of files we are entitled to open: files the user gives the program, and the sample files in the table
   below. An observation says the file and the offsets.
3. rvt-rs's code and documents, under its Apache-2.0 licence, at the commit named below.
4. Autodesk's publicly exported symbol names and its published API constants (the `BuiltInCategory` values such as
   `OST_Walls`). Names and numbers, not behaviour.
5. Autodesk's open-source IFC exporter, `revit-ifc`, to learn what Revit's own IFC export writes. Read, never copied: its code
   is LGPL and would bring that licence in. Part 1 uses none of it.

### Forbidden sources

- Autodesk SDK source, or disassembly or decompilation of Autodesk's binaries beyond their public export names.
- Open Design Alliance SDK source or internals.
- Leaked, breached or NDA material of any kind.
- Copying or translating `revit-ifc`'s code.
- Anyone who has signed an NDA covering Revit internals does not contribute findings that NDA covers.

If a finding's source is not on the accepted list, it does not go in. If one turns out to have come from the forbidden list,
the code goes out, and a different person re-derives it.

1	# The Revit file reader: where every part of it comes from
2	
3	BIMCraft reads Autodesk Revit files (`.rvt`, `.rfa`) with a reader of its own, `crates/rvt` (package `bimcraft-rvt`). Revit's
4	format has no public specification, so [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) and [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md) allow it only under the fence
5	below. This document is the record the fence asks for: every module and every format finding names its source here. A change
6	to the reader that adds a module or a finding adds its row in the same commit (`crates/rvt/src/tests.rs` fails when a source
7	file has no row).
8	
9	## The risk, stated plainly
10	
11	The project owner chose this on 2026-10-21 and accepted the risk below. None of it is a legal conclusion.
12	
13	- The agent that wrote this reader is not a lawyer. It did not verify rvt-rs's claim that its work is clean-room, and it makes
14	  no claim of its own about whether reading Revit's format is lawful in any country, or whether Autodesk's terms for Revit or
15	  for its sample files allow it. Those are the owner's to decide, with counsel if they want it.
16	- rvt-rs has one author. Its `CLEANROOM.md` describes a process (accepted and forbidden sources, a declaration on each pull
17	  request). Whether that process was followed was not audited here, and could not be from the outside.
18	- Some of rvt-rs's findings are second-hand: it credits Discussion #112 of its own repository (a user, STE1200), puzzbobb's
19	  measurements across 30 files, and `ahzs645/reviter`, whose "ODA loader analysis" is named as the independent source of the
20	  stored-page constants in `compression.rs`. What those people used to find them was not checked. Where this reader uses such a
21	  finding, the row says so and says how it was confirmed here (by the bytes of a sample file), which shows the finding is true
22	  and does not show where it came from. The stored-page constants are the exception: they were derived again from the bytes
23	  alone, by someone who had not seen them (see their section below).
24	- Autodesk's sample projects were downloaded from Autodesk's own public download host (see Sample files). Their terms of use
25	  were not checked.
26	
27	## The fence
28	
29	1. **A crate of its own.** `crates/rvt`, package `bimcraft-rvt`, `license = "Apache-2.0"` (not the repository's
30	   MIT OR Apache-2.0, because it holds Apache-2.0 code ported from rvt-rs). `bimcraft-core` never depends on it, and neither
31	   does `crates/update`, `crates/ui-egui` or the MCP server's core path. The command line (`apps/bimcraft-cli`) and the desktop
32	   (`apps/bimcraft`) take it through the Cargo feature `rvt`, which is on by default; a build without it is
33	   `--no-default-features`. A test reads the manifests (`crates/rvt/src/tests.rs`).
34	2. **Attribution, as Apache-2.0 asks.** `crates/rvt/LICENSE` is the licence text; `crates/rvt/NOTICE` carries rvt-rs's
35	   copyright line (Copyright 2026 Griffin Long) and says what was taken; every file with ported code opens with a header that
36	   names the rvt-rs source file and commit and says it was changed. A build that includes the crate is distributed under
37	   Apache-2.0: the README says so, every package (deb, rpm, Arch, AppImage, the AppStream metainfo, the Windows installer and the
38	   macOS bundle) names Apache-2.0, and each ships the root `NOTICE`, which starts with a copy of the crate's (a test keeps it
39	   so) and goes on to the interface fonts' notice.
40	3. **This document.** Every module and every format finding has a source from the accepted list below.
41	4. **Nothing inside an Autodesk file becomes BIMCraft content.** No family, template, icon or help text is bundled, extracted
42	   or shipped. The reader reads a file the user gives it. Test fixtures are synthetic files written by the tests; Autodesk's
43	   files are never committed.
44	5. **The policy documents say so.** CLAUDE.md's clean-room rule and principle 5 of the roadmap point here.
45	
46	### Accepted sources
47	
48	1. Public specifications: MS-CFB (the Compound File Binary format, which Revit files are), RFC 1951 and RFC 1952 (deflate and
49	   gzip), the PNG specification, and for the schema of the model, IFC4 (ISO 16739).
50	2. Byte observations of files we are entitled to open: files the user gives the program, and the sample files in the table
51	   below. An observation says the file and the offsets.
52	3. rvt-rs's code and documents, under its Apache-2.0 licence, at the commit named below.
53	4. Autodesk's publicly exported symbol names and its published API constants (the `BuiltInCategory` values such as
54	   `OST_Walls`). Names and numbers, not behaviour.
55	5. Autodesk's open-source IFC exporter, `revit-ifc`, to learn what Revit's own IFC export writes. Read, never copied: its code
56	   is LGPL and would bring that licence in. Part 1 uses none of it.
57	
58	### Forbidden sources
59	
60	- Autodesk SDK source, or disassembly or decompilation of Autodesk's binaries beyond their public export names.
61	- Open Design Alliance SDK source or internals.
62	- Leaked, breached or NDA material of any kind.
63	- Copying or translating `revit-ifc`'s code.
64	- Anyone who has signed an NDA covering Revit internals does not contribute findings that NDA covers.
65	
66	If a finding's source is not on the accepted list, it does not go in. If one turns out to have come from the forbidden list,
67	the code goes out, and a different person re-derives it.
68

165	| A round pipe's outside diameter is the one its record's box gives: the box of a cylinder of diameter `d`, length `l` along the unit vector `u` is `l\|u\| + d sqrt(1 - u^2)` across on each axis, so `d` is worked out on the axes the pipe is not along (`\|u\| <= 0.8`) and averaged; the nominal diameter is in the data as two equal `f64` 66 and 74 bytes from the data's header, and is smaller than the outside diameter for steel pipes | **Found here**, by comparing the box with the data | the same file: the two nominal numbers are equal and plausible for 4,410 of 4,410 pipes; the box's diameter lies within 0.95 and 1.4 of the nominal one for 4,003 of the 4,408 pipes with both connectors (a DN100 pipe's 0.328 ft nominal against its 0.375 ft box, a DN80's 0.2625 against 0.2917). The import takes the box's, and says so in its notes |
166	| A duct's or a cable tray's data holds its location line as a bounded line (`04 00 08 01`, as a wall's, see above) and, 66 and 74 bytes from the data's header, two `f64` (feet): its width and its height, which are a round duct's diameter twice | **Found here**, by looking for where a duct's box coordinates occur in its data and comparing the two numbers with the box | the workshared Revit 2018 file above: the line and the two numbers are in the data of all 1,194 ducts and all 31 cable trays; of 12 ducts and 6 cable trays looked at by hand, the axis-aligned ones' boxes have the two numbers as their cross-section (a duct 2.2966 by 1.3123 ft standing, a tray 0.164 by 0.328 ft), and a duct turned 45° about its vertical axis has the box its turned section makes (1.9685 by 3.2808 ft in a box 3.71 ft across). A duct whose two numbers are equal is taken as round, which a square duct would also be: not told apart here |
167	| The categories the name table above has not hold, for pipes, pipe fittings, ducts, duct fittings and flex ducts, a companion element each: its record's box is the box of the element it goes with, to the micron, and its id is mostly one above that element's | **Found here**, by comparing the box of each record of a category with no name with the boxes of the records of the named ones | the workshared Revit 2018 file above: 11,664 elements of six categories with no name have exactly the box of an element of a named category (4,410 beside the pipes, 6,132 beside the pipe fittings, 541 beside the ducts, 509 beside the duct fittings, 71 beside the flex ducts, and one more); in the first five, 11,632 of them have the element one to three ids below as the one whose box it is. The import leaves these out and lists them, and does not say what they are: their names are not known here |
168	
169	### The stored-page constants, and where they come from
170	
171	`gzip.rs` has two numbers and a list: a stored page is 65,249 bytes, of which the first 64,896 are data and the last 353 a run
172	that belongs to no gzip member, and the container pages the partitions, the schema and six `Global` streams. The list is
173	rvt-rs's. The two numbers (and so the 353) are derived from the bytes of the samples, by someone who had not seen them.
174	
175	**Why a second derivation.** rvt-rs's `compression.rs` credits the numbers to "ahzs645/reviter's ODA loader analysis and
176	Discussion #112". ODA internals are on the forbidden list and the claim cannot be audited, so the owner had the numbers derived
177	again. A separate agent session did it on 2026-10-21. It was told not to open `gzip.rs`, any other code that handles pages or trailers, the
178	earlier rows and text about them in this document, the part 1 hand-over note, rvt-rs's `compression.rs`, or anything of
179	reviter, ODA or Autodesk until its derivation was written down; it used its own Compound File reader (MS-CFB only), raw inflate
180	(RFC 1951) and the CRC-32 and length at the end of a gzip member (RFC 1952). It wrote its notes first (`derivation.md` and its
181	Python programs, kept with the session notes, not in this repository) and read `gzip.rs` and this document after. The earlier
182	scratch check, which searched a window "chosen around the known answer", is replaced by this.
183	
184	**What it did, on the four samples** (`rstbasicsampleproject.rvt`, 2023 to 2026; all Compound Files of version 4):
185	
186	1. Checked every gzip member as stored (header per RFC 1952, raw inflate, CRC-32 and length). The small streams verify. Every
187	   stream longer than 64,896 bytes does not: in the partition, 300 of 387 members verify in 2023 (324 of 415, 326 of 416 and
188	   322 of 414 in the others), and `Global/Latest`, `Formats/Latest`, `Global/ContentDocuments` and, from 2024,
189	   `Global/ElemTable` fail whole. A failing member can still end exactly at its own trailer with too much output (Huffman codes
190	   resynchronise), so only the CRC and the length count, never "inflate finished".
191	2. Searched for a run to remove, with no prior. In the first member of each sample's partition that zlib rejects, every cut of 1
192	   to 4,096 bytes was tried at every offset up to the byte zlib rejects (a cut at or after it leaves that byte as it was). One
193	   pair makes the member verify, in all four samples: 353 bytes at stream offset 130,145.
194	3. Cut every failing member by 353 bytes, trying every offset: 86 of 87, 91 of 91, 90 of 90 and 92 of 92 are repaired by one
195	   cut at one offset (one offset in each has an equal neighbour); the 87th, in 2023, holds two runs.
196	4. Fitted the spacing: every integer period from 2 to 65,249, the smallest distance between two cuts (two runs cannot be
197	   closer than the period), was tried against all the cuts. Three fit by congruence, 71, 919 and 65,249 (71 x 919 = 65,249); the
198	   first two would put a run through members that verify as stored. The first run ends at 1 x 65,249, so pages count from byte 0
199	   of the stream, the eight-byte prefix of a `Global/*` stream included.
200	5. Without the fitted model: the single-member streams have a unique cut at 64,896 in 2023 `Global/Latest` and 2024
201

# The Revit file reader: where every part of it comes from

BIMCraft reads Autodesk Revit files (`.rvt`, `.rfa`) with a reader of its own, `crates/rvt` (package `bimcraft-rvt`). Revit's
format has no public specification, so [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) and [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md) allow it only under the fence
below. This document is the record the fence asks for: every module and every format finding names its source here. A change
to the reader that adds a module or a finding adds its row in the same commit (`crates/rvt/src/tests.rs` fails when a source
file has no row).

## The risk, stated plainly

The project owner chose this on 2026-10-21 and accepted the risk below. None of it is a legal conclusion.

- The agent that wrote this reader is not a lawyer. It did not verify rvt-rs's claim that its work is clean-room, and it makes
  no claim of its own about whether reading Revit's format is lawful in any country, or whether Autodesk's terms for Revit or
  for its sample files allow it. Those are the owner's to decide, with counsel if they want it.
- rvt-rs has one author. Its `CLEANROOM.md` describes a process (accepted and forbidden sources, a declaration on each pull
  request). Whether that process was followed was not audited here, and could not be from the outside.
- Some of rvt-rs's findings are second-hand: it credits Discussion #112 of its own repository (a user, STE1200), puzzbobb's
  measurements across 30 files, and `ahzs645/reviter`, whose "ODA loader analysis" is named as the independent source of the
  stored-page constants in `compression.rs`. What those people used to find them was not checked. Where this reader uses such a
  finding, the row says so and says how it was confirmed here (by the bytes of a sample file), which shows the finding is true
  and does not show where it came from. The stored-page constants are the exception: they were derived again from the bytes
  alone, by someone who had not seen them (see their section below).
- Autodesk's sample projects were downloaded from Autodesk's own public download host (see Sample files). Their terms of use
  were not checked.

## The fence

1. **A crate of its own.** `crates/rvt`, package `bimcraft-rvt`, `license = "Apache-2.0"` (not the repository's
   MIT OR Apache-2.0, because it holds Apache-2.0 code ported from rvt-rs). `bimcraft-core` never depends on it, and neither
   does `crates/update`, `crates/ui-egui` or the MCP server's core path. The command line (`apps/bimcraft-cli`) and the desktop
   (`apps/bimcraft`) take it through the Cargo feature `rvt`, which is on by default; a build without it is
   `--no-default-features`. A test reads the manifests (`crates/rvt/src/tests.rs`).
2. **Attribution, as Apache-2.0 asks.** `crates/rvt/LICENSE` is the licence text; `crates/rvt/NOTICE` carries rvt-rs's
   copyright line (Copyright 2026 Griffin Long) and says what was taken; every file with ported code opens with a header that
   names the rvt-rs source file and commit and says it was changed. A build that includes the crate is distributed under
   Apache-2.0: the README says so, every package (deb, rpm, Arch, AppImage, the AppStream metainfo, the Windows installer and the
   macOS bundle) names Apache-2.0, and each ships the root `NOTICE`, which starts with a copy of the crate's (a test keeps it
   so) and goes on to the interface fonts' notice.
3. **This document.** Every module and every format finding has a source from the accepted list below.
4. **Nothing inside an Autodesk file becomes BIMCraft content.** No family, template, icon or help text is bundled, extracted
   or shipped. The reader reads a file the user gives it. Test fixtures are synthetic files written by the tests; Autodesk's
   files are never committed.
5. **The policy documents say so.** CLAUDE.md's clean-room rule and principle 5 of the roadmap point here.

### Accepted sources

1. Public specifications: MS-CFB (the Compound File Binary format, which Revit files are), RFC 1951 and RFC 1952 (deflate and
   gzip), the PNG specification, and for the schema of the model, IFC4 (ISO 16739).
2. Byte observations of files we are entitled to open: files the user gives the program, and the sample files in the table
   below. An observation says the file and the offsets.
3. rvt-rs's code and documents, under its Apache-2.0 licence, at the commit named below.
4. Autodesk's publicly exported symbol names and its published API constants (the `BuiltInCategory` values such as
   `OST_Walls`). Names and numbers, not behaviour.
5. Autodesk's open-source IFC exporter, `revit-ifc`, to learn what Revit's own IFC export writes. Read, never copied: its code
   is LGPL and would bring that licence in. Part 1 uses none of it.

### Forbidden sources

- Autodesk SDK source, or disassembly or decompilation of Autodesk's binaries beyond their public export names.
- Open Design Alliance SDK source or internals.
- Leaked, breached or NDA material of any kind.
- Copying or translating `revit-ifc`'s code.
- Anyone who has signed an NDA covering Revit internals does not contribute findings that NDA covers.

If a finding's source is not on the accepted list, it does not go in. If one turns out to have come from the forbidden list,
the code goes out, and a different person re-derives it.

## The reference: rvt-rs

| | |
|---|---|
| Repository | https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs |
| Commit read and ported from | `b6086d41b9758fd9b92f42f0a47b8345b9c58056` (2026-10-21, after the v0.6.1 tag) |
| Licence | Apache-2.0; `NOTICE` says "Copyright 2026 Griffin Long" |
| What it says of its sources | `CLEANROOM.md`: public byte observations, exported symbol names, previously published work (Apache Tika, chuongmep/revit-extractor, phi-ag/rvt), IFC specifications, and `revit-ifc` for what the export writes; forbids SDK source, ODA source, leaked or NDA material, disassembly beyond exports |
| How it was used here | Read for the container, the streams, the schema and the partition records; code ported file by file as the module table says; and built from a scratch clone with its own target directory, to compare its output with this reader's on the same files. It is a measuring stick, never a dependency of this repository |

Its README's legal claims were not copied and are not relied on.

## Modules

| File | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lib.rs` | the crate's documentation and exports | BIMCraft |
| `error.rs` | the errors, each saying what is wrong with the file | BIMCraft |
| `container.rs` | opens a Compound File with limits (file size, stream count, stored size), lists and reads streams, checks it is a Revit file | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/reader.rs` and `src/streams.rs` at `b6086d4`, changed (read on demand instead of loaded whole, one `Limits` struct, no panics). The container itself is MS-CFB, read with the `cfb` crate |
| `gzip.rs` | gzip header, bounded inflate, joining a partition's members, the stored-page constants and which streams are paged | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/compression.rs` at `b6086d4` (the header parse, the list of paged streams, the bounded inflate loop, finding members by their magic), changed (no panics, in-place page stripping, members found by walking from the end of the last one, one inflate cap for a whole stream, trailer checked). The page size and the data in a page are not ported: they are byte observations of the four samples, derived again (see The stored-page constants). The format is RFC 1951 and RFC 1952 |
| `info.rs` | `BasicFileInfo`: release, build, GUID, locale, last saver and path, the `Key: value` block | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/basic_file_info.rs` at `b6086d4`, changed (the block is found by its first line and each line read from its own start; no scoring of two alignments). rvt-rs says the approach matches Apache Tika and chuongmep/revit-extractor, which are public |
| `atom.rs` | the Atom entry of `PartAtom` (families) and of `ProjectInformation` (a one-entry ZIP): title, save time, product version, OmniClass, categories | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/part_atom.rs` and `src/project_information.rs` at `b6086d4`, changed (a small scanner of its own instead of quick-xml, size, depth and tag limits). The ZIP is PKWARE's public APPNOTE; the XML is Atom (RFC 4287) with Autodesk's `urn:schemas-autodesk-com:partatom` elements |
| `preview.rs` | finds and checks the PNG in `RevitPreview4.0` | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/reader.rs` (`preview_png`) at `b6086d4`, changed (every chunk's size and CRC-32 checked, dimensions bounded). The PNG format is the W3C/ISO 15948 specification |
| `schema.rs` | `Formats/Latest`: the list of classes with tag, base, version and field count | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/formats.rs` (`schema_classes`, the grammar reader) at `b6086d4`, changed (class list only, bounds-checked, nesting capped). The grammar is credited by rvt-rs to STE1200 (Discussion #112), whose basis was not checked |
| `elem_table.rs` | the ElementIds `Global/ElemTable` declares, in the 28-byte or 40-byte record layout | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/elem_table.rs` at `b6086d4`, changed (ids only, the ids of both columns, no 12-byte fallback, all counts and offsets checked). rvt-rs credits the frame to STE1200, measured by puzzbobb on 30 files |
| `inventory.rs` | the elements of a project by `BuiltInCategory` (placed instances told from the rest), and its levels with names, elevations, Building Story setting and the levels that sit inside other elements | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_element_records.rs`, `src/partition_element_records_2023.rs` and `src/partition_level_records.rs` (including `building_story_after` and `owned_level_ids`) at `b6086d4`, changed (marker always from the file's schema, bounds-checked offsets, only id, category, class and placed kept, no bounding boxes or reference lists). The category ids are Autodesk's published `BuiltInCategory` constants; the names are rvt-rs's, measured in Revit's own IFC export of sample files |
| `records.rs` | the records of a partition: each element's id, category, class, box and its two reference lists, and the box-less records of types and materials, in both record forms | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_element_records.rs`, `src/partition_element_records_2023.rs` and `src/partition_type_records.rs` at `b6086d4`, changed (every tag from the file's schema, records handed to a callback, one function per form, bounds-checked, every length within `MAX_FEET` (3e5 ft) of zero: BIMCraft's own bound, since Revit's working limit is 20 miles from the origin) |
| `curves.rs` | the bounded line and the arc in an element's data: a wall's location line | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_beam_axes.rs` at `b6086d4` (RE-49, RE-75), changed (only the record readers; every read bounds-checked) |
| `data.rs` | an element's serialised data (header, id, bytes to the next header), the newest copy, a material's name, a category's material in the object styles | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_names.rs`, `src/partition_beam_axes.rs` (`scan_first_records`) and `src/partition_materials.rs` at `b6086d4` (RE-58, RE-91, RE-111, RE-115, RE-116, RE-125, and `src/partition_column_nodes.rs` for a column's geometry node, RE-173), changed (the header and the frame tags from the file's schema; every copy kept with its partition) |
| `types.rs` | a type's name and layers, a wall's orientation, the one type a record names | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_compound_structure.rs`, `src/partition_names.rs` and `src/partition_type_records.rs` at `b6086d4` (RE-28, RE-53, RE-54, RE-111, RE-112), changed (frame tags from the schema, a name only in the type's own data) |
| `walls.rs` | walls: the location line and arc, the side of the exterior, levels and height from the reference list and the box, type and layers | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/element_record_level_refs.rs`, `src/element_record_wall_joins.rs` and `src/partition_compound_structure.rs` at `b6086d4` (RE-27, RE-29, RE-54, RE-59), changed (builds BIMCraft's parametric wall; its ends are the line's and BIMCraft joins walls where they meet) |
| `sketch.rs` | a sketched element's boundary: its sketch lines (a curve each) closed into regions and their voids, by the curves' ends or, before 2024, by their boxes | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/element_record_plan_profiles.rs` and `src/partition_beam_axes.rs` (`first_sketch_curve`) at `b6086d4` (RE-25, RE-50, RE-96), changed (one tracer for both ways, arcs drawn as chords within 0.5 mm, every size capped) |
| `floors.rs` | floors and ceilings: the sketch, the one type the reference list names, the level, the offset | BIMCraft, from the findings above (rvt-rs `element_record_level_refs.rs` for the levels, RE-27, RE-59) |
| `names.rs` | the name entries of families and family types (up to 2023 and from 2024), and an id's value in its newest partition | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_names.rs` at `b6086d4` (RE-38, RE-109, RE-145), changed (both forms in one module, the newest partition's entry wins) |
| `openings.rs` | doors and windows: the host wall, the hole as the instance's box along the wall, the type by its name entry, overlapping neighbours fitted | BIMCraft, from the findings below (rvt-rs `partition_schema_mvp.rs` `opening_instances_from_records` and `bind_opening_hosts` for the host rule, RE-23, RE-85) |
| `placement.rs` | a family instance's placement in its data: a rotation and an origin | Ported in part from rvt-rs `src/partition_instance_transforms.rs` at `b6086d4` (RE-87), changed (the bytes of one instance's data, bounds-checked) |
| `columns.rs` | columns, architectural and structural: place and size from the box (the symbol's envelope when turned), levels and height as a wall's, type by its name entry | BIMCraft, from the findings below (rvt-rs `element_record_column_cuts.rs`, `partition_column_nodes.rs`, RE-26, RE-173) |
| `pipes.rs` | pipes: the line between the origins of the two connectors in the data, the outside diameter worked out from the record box, the level below the start | BIMCraft, from the findings below (the bytes of a Revit 2018 file the project owner gave; nothing of this is in rvt-rs) |
| `ducts.rs` | ducts and cable trays: the bounded line of the data as the run's line, its width and height from two numbers in the data | BIMCraft, from the findings below (the bytes of a Revit 2018 file the project owner gave; the bounded line is `curves.rs`'s, ported from rvt-rs) |
| `generic.rs` | the other placed elements (fittings, fixtures, equipment, terminals, generic models) and those of a category the name table has not: a box-shaped component of a family of their category (of the category's id for the latter), from the record's box; an element of a category with no name whose box is a named element's is left out | BIMCraft (nothing new is read from the file: the record's box and its category; the companion rule is the last finding below) |
| `roofs.rs` | roofs by footprint (flat ones only) and by extrusion (a straight-line profile in a plane square to an axis, checked against the record box) | BIMCraft, from the findings above (rvt-rs `partition_roof_slopes.rs`, RE-56, is not ported: no roof of the samples sets an edge's slope; rvt-rs does not read roofs by extrusion at all, so that half is read from the bytes of the sample, see the finding below) |
| `rooms.rs` | rooms: number, name, level, and a point the imported walls enclose | BIMCraft, from the findings below (rvt-rs `partition_room_parameters.rs`, RE-117) |
| `import.rs` | a Revit project read into a `bimcraft-core` model: the levels, the elements by kind, the check-and-drop loop that leaves out what breaks a model rule and says why | BIMCraft, following the pattern of `bimcraft-core`'s IFC importer (`import::ifc`) |
| `project_fixture.rs` | a synthetic project (element table, schema, partition records in both forms, levels with name blocks) for tests | BIMCraft, written from the layouts in `inventory.rs` |
| `fixture.rs` | synthetic Compound Files, gzip members, paged and partition streams, `BasicFileInfo`, ZIP, PNG and schema bytes for tests | BIMCraft |

## Format findings

| Finding | Source | Confirmed here on |
|---|---|---|
| A Revit file is a Compound File (signature `D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1`) with a `BasicFileInfo` stream | MS-CFB; rvt-rs `reader.rs` | the four samples |
| The streams of a project: `BasicFileInfo`, `Contents`, `Formats/Latest`, `Global/{ContentDocuments, DocumentIncrementTable, ElemTable, History, Latest, PartitionTable}`, `Partitions/NN`, `ProjectInformation`, `TransmissionData` (a family has `PartAtom` instead of `ProjectInformation`) | rvt-rs `streams.rs` | the four samples list exactly these 12 |
| The number NN of the partition is not fixed by the release: rvt-rs's table gives 66 to 69 for 2023 to 2026, the samples have 20, 21, 20 and 21. The reader finds partitions by the `Partitions/` prefix | byte observation | the four samples |
| A `Global/*` stream is eight bytes and then one gzip member; `Formats/Latest` starts with its member at byte 0 | rvt-rs `compression.rs` (`inflate_at_auto`); observation | the four samples (the member is found in the first 256 bytes) |
| A partition is a 44-byte header and then gzip members of about 128 KiB of output each, with 40 bytes between one and the next: the previous member's CRC-32 and length, then 32 bytes of header the reader does not read; in 52 gaps of each sample there are 188 more bytes (a small structured item with UTF-16 text and length fields, 228 bytes between the members in all) | byte observation (rvt-rs finds members by scanning for the magic and does not describe the gap) | the four samples: the first member at byte 44, 40 bytes between members in 334 of 386, 362 of 414, 363 of 415 and 361 of 413 gaps and 228 in the 52 others, with the pages' runs taken out. The reader does not depend on the 44, the 40 or the 228 |
| The container stores the schema, the `Global` gzip streams and the partitions in pages of 65,249 bytes, counted from byte 0 of the stream: 64,896 of data and a 353-byte run that belongs to no gzip member; inflate runs on the stream with the runs removed | byte observation of the four samples, derived without the numbers (see The stored-page constants). The same numbers are in rvt-rs `compression.rs`, which credits `ahzs645/reviter`'s analysis of a loader and its Discussion #112 (their basis was not checked, see the risk) | the CRC-32 and length of **every** gzip member of every such stream match once the runs are removed, 1,660 members on four samples (1,664 with the four `Contents` members, under a page). A number wrong by one byte breaks hundreds of them |
| The gzip members are standard, with CRC-32 and length after the deflate stream; rvt-rs calls Revit's streams "truncated" (no trailer). The reader accepts both and reports how many members carried a matching trailer | observation | all 1,660 members of the four samples carry a matching trailer. A file with truncated members is only covered by a synthetic test |
| `BasicFileInfo` is a binary head and then a block of `Key: value` lines in UTF-16LE separated by CR LF, starting at the line `Worksharing:` (some releases put it at an odd byte offset); the value of `IsSingleUserCloudModel` is a narrow `\0False\0` inside the wide text; the stream's last line ends in a narrow CR LF; `Format:` (2019 and later) or `Revit Build: Autodesk Revit 2016 (Build: ...)` (2016 to 2018) gives the release | rvt-rs `basic_file_info.rs`, which says the approach is the one Apache Tika and chuongmep/revit-extractor use. The narrow CR LF at the end is not in rvt-rs: found here | the four samples: all 18 lines of each read, in file order, the same keys on every release. The 2016 to 2018 form and a block at an odd offset are only covered by synthetic tests |
| `Username` is empty unless the file is workshared; the saved path (`Last Save Path`) is the saving machine's, with its user folder in it | byte observation | the four samples (the user folder is in the path; `Username` is empty). `info` shows both and nothing writes them into a project or an IFC file |
| `ProjectInformation` is a ZIP archive with one deflated entry holding the Atom entry (title, update time, `A:product-version`); the entry's name is a temporary path with the saving user's folder in it, so the reader skips it | rvt-rs `project_information.rs` | the four samples (title `rstbasicsampleproject`, product version equal to the release) |
| A family's `PartAtom` is the same Atom entry as plain XML; its OmniClass code is a category term of dotted digits | rvt-rs `part_atom.rs` | **not confirmed on a real file** (the samples are projects): synthetic test only |
| `RevitPreview4.0` is a wrapper of about 300 bytes and then a PNG | rvt-rs `reader.rs` | **not confirmed on a real file**: the four sample projects have no such stream. Synthetic test only |

### The stored-page constants, and where they come from

`gzip.rs` has two numbers and a list: a stored page is 65,249 bytes, of which the first 64,896 are data and the last 353 a run
that belongs to no gzip member, and the container pages the partitions, the schema and six `Global` streams. The list is
rvt-rs's. The two numbers (and so the 353) are derived from the bytes of the samples, by someone who had not seen them.

**Why a second derivation.** rvt-rs's `compression.rs` credits the numbers to "ahzs645/reviter's ODA loader analysis and
Discussion #112". ODA internals are on the forbidden list and the claim cannot be audited, so the owner had the numbers derived
again. A separate agent session did it on 2026-10-21. It was told not to open `gzip.rs`, any other code that handles pages or trailers, the
earlier rows and text about them in this document, the part 1 hand-over note, rvt-rs's `compression.rs`, or anything of
reviter, ODA or Autodesk until its derivation was written down; it used its own Compound File reader (MS-CFB only), raw inflate
(RFC 1951) and the CRC-32 and length at the end of a gzip member (RFC 1952). It wrote its notes first (`derivation.md` and its
Python programs, kept with the session notes, not in this repository) and read `gzip.rs` and this document after. The earlier
scratch check, which searched a window "chosen around the known answer", is replaced by this.

**What it did, on the four samples** (`rstbasicsampleproject.rvt`, 2023 to 2026; all Compound Files of version 4):

1. Checked every gzip member as stored (header per RFC 1952, raw inflate, CRC-32 and length). The small streams verify. Every
   stream longer than 64,896 bytes does not: in the partition, 300 of 387 members verify in 2023 (324 of 415, 326 of 416 and
   322 of 414 in the others), and `Global/Latest`, `Formats/Latest`, `Global/ContentDocuments` and, from 2024,
   `Global/ElemTable` fail whole. A failing member can still end exactly at its own trailer with too much output (Huffman codes
   resynchronise), so only the CRC and the length count, never "inflate finished".
2. Searched for a run to remove, with no prior. In the first member of each sample's partition that zlib rejects, every cut of 1
   to 4,096 bytes was tried at every offset up to the byte zlib rejects (a cut at or after it leaves that byte as it was). One
   pair makes the member verify, in all four samples: 353 bytes at stream offset 130,145.
3. Cut every failing member by 353 bytes, trying every offset: 86 of 87, 91 of 91, 90 of 90 and 92 of 92 are repaired by one
   cut at one offset (one offset in each has an equal neighbour); the 87th, in 2023, holds two runs.
4. Fitted the spacing: every integer period from 2 to 65,249, the smallest distance between two cuts (two runs cannot be
   closer than the period), was tried against all the cuts. Three fit by congruence, 71, 919 and 65,249 (71 x 919 = 65,249); the
   first two would put a run through members that verify as stored. The first run ends at 1 x 65,249, so pages count from byte 0
   of the stream, the eight-byte prefix of a `Global/*` stream included.
5. Without the fitted model: the single-member streams have a unique cut at 64,896 in 2023 `Global/Latest` and 2024
